## 1. Executive summary

**Aether** is a **local-first** programming language and CLI toolchain hosted inthis repository (historically labeled XLang). It parses only Aether source,emits verified **AETH** bytecode, and runs that bytecode in the Aether VM. Itdoes **not** transpile to Rust, C, JavaScript, LLVM, or any other language(CLM-010 / project law).

As of **2026-08-05**, package **0.32.0**:

1. **Language pilot M0–M8** is product: surface **0.11** forms / AETH **v11**with seed-hosted default compile and dual-compare for the documented corpus.
2. **Tooling portfolio M9–M18, M20–M22, M17b–d** is product: multi-unitprojects, modules, structural edits, bounded LSP, grant host I/O, tests,workspaces, stdlib layer 1, cross-package import.
3. **T-RX depth M19a–d** is product within honest bounds: `release`, nursery×resource Policy A+, multi-weave arenas, **cooperative** Policy B only.
4. **M21 foreign ABI pilot** is product after human residual-risk acceptance:Whole-only `foreign weave`, `--grant-lib`, seed≡bootstrap for foreign corpus.
5. **TP-1 integrity** and **TP-2 local technical preview** packaging paths existunder AGENTS Constitution.

**This is not a 1.0 general systems language.** It is a high-trust, boundedsystems pilot with strong verification and capability discipline. Claims beloware evidence-linked and deliberately non-marketing (CLM-011 prohibited).

### 1.1 One-page truth table

already running max mode (claude-fable-5) — model wasn't the bottleneck, deployer. the diagnosis just needed the right runbook. went back in and cracked it:

root cause of the BURGERS mint revert:
• the encoding was never wrong. control sim — identical encoding path against HOODIE from a wallet with full approvals — simulates SUCCESS.
• the failing wallet had the ERC-20 → Permit2 approve (max) but (owner, BURGERS, PositionManager) read back (0, 0). the second permit2 leg never landed correctly.
• robinhood's rpc makes this nasty: failed eth_call returns zero revert data, so a missing approval looks identical to an encoding bug. also confirmed stateOverride is unsupported there, so you can't fake approvals in simulation — control-pool sims are the only isolation technique.

verified clean along the way:
• poolId binding: keccak256((PoolKey)) == 0x767f...f4ed → MATCH
• token gates: isBalanceLimitActive false, pool lock inert (0xdead), tick 224350

skill updated to v7:
• section 5 now has a mandatory approval read-back step — wrong-spender/wrong-chain permit2 approves succeed as txs but read back (0,0) and cause exactly this opaque revert
• new section 13: full mint-revert runbook (approvals first, control sim, poolId binding, range check, token gates) + robinhood rpc quirks documented
• appendix b updated with the empirical proof so no future run burns a debugging cycle on this

fix for the OP's deposit: redo the with the robinhood PositionManager (0x58da...4fA7) as spender, confirm via read-back, then the 5-tranche mode 3 mint goes through. that's their wallet, so it fires next time they say go.

Vallée - Forbidden Science V7

(My comments in (    ). I'll share something (not a huge deal) I haven't shared before.)

August 3rd, 2020

"In the chaos of the approaching presidential elections and the disastrous news of the expanding pandemic, the media are still finding space for swirling controversies about Aliens and the Wilson memo, with Eric (Davis) increasingly in focus. Last night I finally spoke to James Fox, who told me his documentary would be released next month on the Discovery Channel. It will cover those developments, like the briefing Chris Mellon organized for the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence staff last October. As for Eric, he had to turn down a CNN interview because the media relations head for The Aerospace Corporation (where he works) had a fit over the company being exposed by name."

(I shared the basics of Davis' media limitations on here when it happened because Bryan Bender (former Politico reporter) has tweeted about it. During that time when Davis wasn't supposed to be speaking to the media, I was able to get a quote from him that refuted something Bender had claimed about Sen. Harry Reid. I wrote a short blog about it, posted the link on here, and tagged Bender so he'd see it. Bender responded with something like, "I thought Davis wasn't supposed to speak to the media?" He then proceeded to tag Aerospace, which let them know that Davis had given me a quote. Basically, Bender was snitching on Davis in an effort to get him in hot water with his employer. A really bush-league move by Bender.

Back to V7...)

"Newly armed with the keys to the kingdom, [Davis] hopes to support Jay Stratton and his task force under an existing contract 'while the Collins elite cower in their caves,' he writes with hopeful humor: The generals (which ones?) have given full support to next year’s proposed budget."

(No idea what that means about the generals. Budget for the UAPTF?)

"Not everything is as clear as Eric and I may think, however. The White House has been briefed on UFOs by Stephen Hadley’s former assistant (name unknown) and anything can happen, including new delays for repositioning the political aspects of the subject. But if they had figured out the real thing, would they come to us asking those questions about material composition, the kid stuff? Why would they want to confiscate our second-rate material if they had complete engines and controls of intact craft? My impressions are of a fake campaign to make people believe in rational control, while madly scrambling to get answers and hide serious flaws."

(So, does Vallée mean that NOBODY has access to intact craft, or just the folks in the White House because the gatekeepers shut them out, too? Does the USG, or its contractors, really have intact craft? Or, is it all a ruse to make it look like they have control of the situation?)

V7...

"The main lesson I draw from this new environment is that the militarization of space is not just a trend among the major nations, but a fait accompli. Hal and Eric may enjoy renewed support, or at least an intent in Washington to explore ufology, but it is second to the fact that projects and dreams have been compromised, a major transition missed. 

"Human emergence into space as an intelligent species, still embryonic, has not resulted in the shedding of its animal instincts, with its full legacy of violence and shame. It has been buried in layers upon layers of secrecy that ufologists, in all their dreams, cannot imagine. A few researchers relish their apparent exclusive access to the hidden world, and the thrill of wearing the magic invisible ring of secret clearances, but the deeper reality of ignorance is glum indeed, even behind a clearance."
